title: Speak: first phrases
description: Sound first. Say useful phrases before you can read them.

units.title: Hello and goodbye
intro: This path is sound first. Phrases are shown in pinyin so you can say them. The characters are shown small underneath.
Tones matter for being understood. If you have not done 'The four tones' in the reading path, do it first or right after this.
Tap the speaker, listen for how the voice moves, and repeat out loud.

items.hint: Sounds like 'nee how'. Two dipping tones in a row are hard to say, so the first one rises instead.
Close to 'dzow-shahng how'. z sounds like the 'ds' in 'kids'.
Close to 'dzai jyen'. Both syllables fall sharply. It means 'see you again'.

units.title: Thanks and sorry
intro: Two pairs: a phrase, and the usual answer to it.
In pinyin, x is a soft 'sh' and q is a soft 'ch', both made with the tongue flat behind the lower teeth.

items.hint: Close to 'shyeh-shyeh'. The first one falls, the second is light.
Close to 'boo kuh-chee'. The usual answer to 谢谢.
Close to 'dway-boo-chee'. For a real apology.
Close to 'may gwahn-shee'. The usual answer to 'sorry': no problem.

units.title: Getting by
intro: Phrases for shops and for moments when you are lost.
Mandarin has no single word for 'yes'. You repeat the verb. 是 means 'it is', and 不是 means 'it is not'.

items.hint: Close to 'ching' with a dipping tone. Put it before a request.
Close to 'shr' with a sharp fall. It means 'it is'.
Close to 'waw boo dong'. 我 is I, 不 is not, 懂 is understand.
Close to 'dwaw-shao chyen'. 钱 means money.
